decision.summary: The Fed held its policy rate at 5.25% to 5.5%. The vote was 12-0.

changes.quote: Recent indicators suggest that economic activity has continued to expand at a solid pace.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Recent indicators suggest that economic activity has been expanding at a solid pace.”

changes.quote: In recent months, there has been a lack of further progress toward the Committee's 2 percent inflation objective.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: The Committee judges that the risks to achieving its employment and inflation goals have moved toward better balance over the past year.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “The Committee judges that the risks to achieving its employment and inflation goals are moving into better balance.”

changes.quote: In addition, the Committee will continue reducing its holdings of Treasury securities and agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “In addition, the Committee will continue reducing its holdings of Treasury securities and agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities, as described in its…”

changes.quote: Beginning in June, the Committee will slow the pace of decline of its securities holdings by reducing the monthly redemption cap on Treasury securities from $60 billion to $25 billion.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: The Committee will maintain the monthly redemption cap on agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities at $35 billion and will reinvest any principal payments in excess of this cap into Treasury securities.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

tone_quotes.quote: The Committee does not expect it will be appropriate to reduce the target range until it has gained greater confidence that inflation is moving sustainably toward 2 percent.
The Committee is strongly committed to returning inflation to its 2 percent objective.
The economic outlook is uncertain, and the Committee remains highly attentive to inflation risks.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 21.47% APR costs about $89.46 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 4.63% and moved -6 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 7.1% would fall by about $12.12 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 3.9%, and employers added an average of 203k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 3.5% over the past year (March 2024); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 3.1%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 1.4% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -8 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved -0.34%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.03% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is hawkish (leaning toward higher rates). The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 95%, cut 4%, hike 0%.

citations.detail: In support of its goals, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent.
